subject: Unit-rate reconciliation and host-rate snapshot
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@clearhealth.com>, Tim Owens <tim.owens@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unit-rate reconciliation and host-rate snapshot

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and some clear signals on volume and cost expectations. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before I put together a short commercial note: 

Demo recap
- We walked through the inference flow for ClearHealth’s patient-summarization pipeline (30–90s documents, typical context window ~1k tokens).
- You confirmed the primary production use-case is triage summarization + clinical search enrichment (no PHI will be sent in initial pilot; production plan will use our Private deployment).

Key numbers we captured (please confirm/correct)
- Expected pilot volume: 10M–30M tokens / month (ramp to 30M in 3 months)
- Annualized run rate target after pilot: 100M+/mo (longer-term)
- Budget signal: mid-range procurement budget; you mentioned wanting unit economics in the ballpark that keep monthly spend within your budget envelope for pilot (we discussed $/1M targets below).

Pricing / $ per 1M tokens question (ask for you)
- You flagged an internal goal of landing unit cost around $60–90 per 1M tokens for the pilot (you said that would be comfortable given quality), and that procurement would want a 3-tier option if we scale. Can you confirm that range?

Immediate next steps
- Mateo → draft a 1-page commercial note with 3-tier unit pricing (pilot / production / committed) + cost levers (batching, KV cache, quantization tradeoffs). Attached: redwood-1m-estimate.xlsx (cost model) + MOA stub for procurement to review.
- Sarah/Tim → confirm target $/1M range and whether we should include an option for a short-term volume discount.
- Internal: loop in Ben (SE) and Laura (AE) to validate the cost model and a pragmatic canary plan for the pilot.

Attachments: redwood-1m-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet with sample per-model costs and example monthly totals), ClearHealth_MOA_v1.pdf (procurement stub).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the commercial note by EOD Monday.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com

From: Tim Owens <tim.owens@clearhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@clearhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unit-rate reconciliation and host-rate snapshot

Thanks Mateo — summary looks accurate. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Volume profile
- Pilot: likely start at ~8–12M tokens / month but we have predictable weekly spikes (end of month batch enrichments) up to ~25–30M in peak weeks.

2) Budget + unit target
- Our target for the pilot is $60–90 / 1M tokens — lower end preferred if the output fidelity and latency meet our SLAs. That maps to a ballpark pilot budget of $480–$1,080 / month initially (depending on consumption). If the pilot proves out, we can expand to the mid-five-figures monthly.

3) Procurement asks
- We’ll need a one-page SOW + pricing schedule; procurement will want an explicit line for data retention/audit logs and a simple SLA for latency.

We’re keen to see a concrete 3-tier that shows USD per 1M token for (pilot / production / committed) plus an example monthly total.

Tim
Tim Owens
Director, Platform Engineering — ClearHealth
tim.owens@clearhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unit-rate reconciliation and host-rate snapshot

Copying our internal bench notes — want to propose an approach before Mateo sends the public-facing commercial note: 

Bench / quick market snapshot (approx, model-dependent):
- OpenAI (hosted): ~ $120 / 1M (for the larger conversational models we’d compare against) — high variability based on context window and temperature.
- Anthropic (hosted): ~ $95 / 1M for similar capability tiers.
- Self-hosted / open-model hosts (quantized 8-bit on A100 / V100-backed infra): effective cost can be in the $30–60 / 1M range once you apply batching + KV cache — but this requires conservative quality and operational ownership.

Implications for ClearHealth
- They’ve signaled $60–90 / 1M which sits between the open-host low and the hosted incumbents. That gives us an opportunity to position Redwood as: production-grade (SLA & security) + lower unit economics than OpenAI/Anthropic for comparable quality via our Dedicated/Private offerings.

Recommendation (what to include in Mateo’s note)
- A simple 3-tier price table: Pilot: $85 / 1M (month-to-month, no commit), Production: $60 / 1M (3–6 month commit), Committed: $45 / 1M (12 month + reserved capacity) — include a footnote showing how batching, cache, and quantization can move effective unit costs.
- Highlight fallbacks: automatic routing to a cheaper quantized variant if capacity/price policy triggers.
- Include an example monthly calc for 10M and 30M tokens so procurement sees the delta.

I’ll draft the numbers into the spreadsheet and run a short sensitivity (attached in Mateo’s file). If we want to be aggressive, we can set pilot at $75 / 1M and offer a one-time pilot credit to get initial consumption visible. Thoughts?

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@clearhealth.com>, Tim Owens <tim.owens@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unit-rate reconciliation and host-rate snapshot

Appreciate the quick clarifications Tim. We’ll turn this into a tight one-pager and a 3-tier price table (Ben’s recommendation above is what we’ll start with).

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute pricing + SOW sync to walk through the commercial note and the SLA/retention lines — Tue Aug 3, 10:00 AM PT (I’ve linked a tentative HubSpot calendar below; if that time doesn’t work, please propose alternatives).

HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/meetings/mateo/clearhealth-pricing-sync

Action items (owners)
- Mateo: send 1-page commercial note + revised spreadsheet (today EOD).
- Ben: finalize the sensitivity tab + proposed pilot credit line.
- Laura: prepare an internal procurement-facing SOW stub (SLA, data retention, audit logs).
- Sarah/Tim: confirm meeting time and the $60–90 / 1M pilot target (or correct).

Thanks — talk soon.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
